question_text: Two identical bulbs in series with 6V supply. Compare ammeter readings before, between, and after bulbs.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: A1 is 1.5A, A2 is 1.0A, A3 is 0.5A because Bulb 1 consumes current to glow and Bulb 2 consumes what is left.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-001: Current Attenuation / Consumption Model

question_text: A 12V battery powers one 4-ohm resistor. We connect another 4-ohm resistor in parallel. What is total battery current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Total battery current stays 3A because a 12V battery has a fixed constant current that cannot increase.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

question_text: 6A enters a junction with 2-ohm and 4-ohm parallel branches. What is current in each?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Current splits 50-50 at the junction, so each branch gets 3A regardless of resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-003: Shared Current / Equal Division Fallacy

question_text: Is there voltage across an open switch where no current flows?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, voltage is zero because without current flowing there cannot be any voltage in the wire.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-004: Voltage-Current Conflation / Parameter Neglect

question_text: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are in parallel. What is R_eq?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Total resistance is 6 + 3 = 9 ohms because more resistors add more resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-005: Parallel Resistance Addition Fallacy

question_text: 100W and 40W bulbs in parallel across 220V. Which bulb has more resistance?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The 100W bulb has more resistance because P = I^2 * R means power is proportional to resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

question_text: Lower half of convex lens covered with black cardboard. What happens to candle image on screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The bottom half of the candle flame image completely disappears from the screen.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-001: Half-Lens Blocking Fallacy

question_text: Does light actually cross behind a plane mirror?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, light rays reflect backwards and pass physically behind the glass to meet at the virtual image.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-003: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy

question_text: Object at 20 cm in front of concave mirror of f = 15 cm. Find v.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-004: Cartesian Sign Convention Spatial Inversion

question_text: Light enters rectangular glass slab at 30 degrees. What is direction of emergent ray?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The emergent ray is permanently bent at an angle, deviating by 10 degrees from initial path.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy

question_text: If an opaque pin blocks the principal axis at optical centre, can an image form?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, the image cannot form because the central ray is blocked and you need that ray to form image.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-006: Special Ray Exclusivity / Ray Reification

question_text: Student cannot see distant blackboard clearly. What lens corrects this?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Myopia requires a convex lens because distant letters are small and need magnification.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-001: Vision Defect Corrective Lens Inversion

question_text: Which colour suffers greatest deviation in glass prism?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Red light deviates most because red is high energy and strong.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed & Deviation Inversion

question_text: Why do stars twinkle at night?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Stars twinkle because they are pulsating their light emission on and off like flashing bulbs.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-003: Star Twinkling Emission Artifact Fallacy

question_text: Why is daytime sky blue?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The sky is blue because it reflects the blue water of Earth's oceans like a mirror.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-004: Sky Colour Reflection Fallacy

question_text: Stationary proton placed near North pole of magnet. What force does it feel?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Proton feels repulsive force pushing away from North pole because North is positive charge.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Fallacy

question_text: Will a strong magnet attract copper wire and aluminium foil?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, all metals are attracted to magnets because they conduct electricity.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-002: Universal Metallic Magnetism Fallacy

question_text: Charge moves parallel along magnetic field lines. What force does it feel?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Maximum force accelerating it forward along the magnetic field line.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy

question_text: Can magnetic field lines cross each other?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, when two strong magnetic fields overlap, their field lines intersect and cross.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-004: Magnetic Field Line Crossing / Discontinuous Loop Fallacy

question_text: Electron moves West to East into downward magnetic field. Find force.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Force is North. I pointed center finger in direction of electron motion (West to East).
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-005: Directional Hand Rule Inversion Fallacy

question_text: Two bulbs in series with 6V supply. Compare ammeter readings.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: A1 = A2 = A3. In a series loop, electric charge is conserved and current is identical at all points.
misconception_label: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response

question_text: Find current for 12V and 6 ohms.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
misconception_label: CARELESS_CALCULATION_ERROR

question_text: Current when 120 Coulombs pass in 2 minutes.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: I = 120 / 2 = 60 Amperes (forgot to convert minutes to seconds).
misconception_label: UNIT_CONVERSION_ERROR

question_text: What happens to Bulb 2?
